page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: Isobars are the curves obtained when the volume
of a gas is plotted against its temperature at
steps.why: Iso means same and bar means pressure: one curve collects all the V–T states of the gas that share one pressure.
common_mistakes: Confusing this isobar with the isobars of Atomic Structure (equal mass number). In this chapter isobar is a constant-pressure curve.
steps.memory_tip: Bar is a unit of pressure, so iso-bar means same pressure.
steps.margin_note: Axes (V against T) plus constant pressure make the definition.

steps.label: The constant quantity and the law

lines.text: Isobar: a V–T curve of a gas at constant pressure

lines: Charles' law (V ∝ T) is the behaviour along one
isobar: for an ideal gas it is a straight line.
steps.why: Along an isobar V ∝ T, which is Charles' law, so the ideal-gas isobar is a straight line on the V–T plot. Naming the law shows the curve is understood, not memorised.
common_mistakes: Attaching Boyle's law here. Boyle's law belongs to constant temperature.
steps.memory_tip: Constant P goes with Charles' law: V grows in step with T along every isobar.
steps.margin_note: The straight-line remark is the detail an examiner rewards.

insider_note: The word isobar appears in two chapters with two meanings — the examiner in THIS chapter expects the constant-pressure V–T curve, not equal mass numbers.
